headline: Russian Zero-Click Exploits, Iranian ICS Attacks, and Critical Zero-Day Patches
summary: This intelligence brief for July 23, 2026, covers a major Russian state-sponsored espionage campaign using a zero-click Zimbra exploit to target Western organizations. U.S. agencies have also expanded warnings about Iranian-affiliated actors targeting industrial control systems from Siemens and Schneider Electric. Additionally, critical zero-day vulnerabilities in Check Point and Microsoft SharePoint products are under active attack, prompting CISA to mandate urgent patching. Other major developments include a large-scale data breach at Paidwork, a new ransomware strain from the Chaos group, and a GAO report on duplicative federal cyber regulations.

articles.headline: Ransomware attack on Coca-Cola's Fairlife halts U.S. milk production
articles.title: Fairlife Halts Production After Ransomware Attack
articles.excerpt: Fairlife, a dairy subsidiary of The Coca-Cola Company, has suspended all U.S. production after a ransomware attack compromised its IT and operational technology networks. The breach was detected on July 16, 2026, leading to an immediate shutdown of affected systems and the launch of an incident response investigation with external experts and law enforcement. While products currently in stores are deemed safe, the halt in production at plants across the U.S. could lead to product shortages. The identity of the threat actor and the full financial impact are not yet known.
articles.updateSummary: Anubis ransomware group claims responsibility for Fairlife attack, alleging 1 TB data exfiltration and Nutanix infrastructure encryption.
articles.updateContent: The Anubis ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the attack on Fairlife, a Coca-Cola subsidiary. The group listed Fairlife on its dark web leak site on July 20, 2026, alleging the encryption of the company's Nutanix infrastructure and the exfiltration of 1 terabyte of confidential data. Anubis is known for its double-extortion tactics and has threatened to leak the stolen data if a ransom is not paid by July 27, 2026. This new development confirms the threat actor and adds a significant data breach component to the incident, escalating the potential impact beyond operational disruption.

articles.headline: Supply Chain Attacks Hit 26% of UK Businesses in the Last Year
articles.title: 1 in 4 UK Firms Hit by Supply Chain Attacks
articles.excerpt: A survey by Databarracks reveals that one in four (26%) UK businesses have suffered a cyber incident originating from their supply chain in the past 12 months. The 'Data Health Check 2026' report highlights a concerning trend: 48% of IT decision-makers admit to knowingly working with suppliers that have security or resilience issues. This is often driven by a strong dependence on these suppliers, which 26% of respondents cited as a major barrier to improving their own organization's security posture. The findings underscore that while awareness of supply chain risk is high, practical and business constraints often prevent organizations from effectively mitigating it, even as cyberattacks remain the top cause of IT downtime.
articles.updateSummary: New statistics reveal organizations knowingly working with risky suppliers are four times more likely to suffer a breach, with added compliance guidance.
articles.updateContent: A new analysis from the Databarracks 'Data Health Check 2026' report highlights a critical finding: organizations that knowingly engage with suppliers having security or resilience issues are over four times more likely to experience a third-party cyber incident (43% vs. 10%). The report also notes that 23% of IT leaders rank supply chain vulnerabilities as a top-three operational challenge for the next five years. This update provides crucial compliance guidance, emphasizing continuous monitoring, tiered risk management, contractual obligations, and the development of exit strategies for critical suppliers, aligning with evolving regulations like DORA and CIRCIA.

articles.headline: Russian APT 'Laundry Bear' Targets West with Zero-Click Zimbra Exploit
articles.title: Russian APT Uses Zero-Click Zimbra Flaw in Espionage Campaign
articles.excerpt: An international advisory details a long-running espionage campaign by the Russian state-sponsored group 'Laundry Bear' (TA488). The actors are exploiting a zero-click vulnerability (CVE-2025-66376) in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite to steal emails and credentials from government, defense, and other critical sector organizations in the U.S. and allied nations. The campaign, active since July 2025, uses a custom tool called 'Ulej' for data exfiltration and has successfully compromised over 10 organizations.

articles.headline: Iranian Hackers Expand Attacks to Siemens, Schneider Industrial Systems
articles.title: US Warns of Iranian Attacks on Siemens & Schneider ICS Devices
articles.excerpt: An updated U.S. government advisory warns that Iranian-affiliated threat actors have expanded their cyber campaigns against U.S. critical infrastructure. The attackers are now targeting internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (PLCs) from Schneider Electric and Siemens, in addition to previously reported Rockwell Automation devices. The actors use legitimate manufacturer software to connect to misconfigured PLCs, override safety logic, and disrupt operations in sectors like water and energy.

articles.headline: Federal Cyber Rules Burden Industry with Duplicative Reporting: GAO
articles.title: GAO Finds Federal Cyber Rules Overlap, Burdening Industry
articles.excerpt: A U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) report finds that federal cybersecurity regulations are creating a significant burden on the private sector due to widespread overlap. The report identified 117 regulations from 37 agencies, with 70% imposing duplicative reporting requirements. This redundancy increases compliance costs and creates inconsistencies for critical infrastructure operators. The findings come as CISA prepares to implement new rules under CIRCIA, potentially adding to the complexity without effective harmonization led by the ONCD.

articles.headline: Google Launches Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber for Vulnerability Hunting
articles.title: Google Unveils Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber AI for Security
articles.excerpt: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a specialized AI model designed for rapid vulnerability discovery and patching. Integrated into the CodeMender AI agent, the model is lightweight and optimized for high-speed code analysis. Citing significant dual-use risks, Google is restricting initial access to a limited pilot program for governments and trusted partners, highlighting the growing industry concern over managing powerful offensive AI tools.

articles.headline: Chaos Ransomware Uses Browser-Based 'msaRAT' to Evade Detection
articles.title: Chaos Ransomware Hides C2 Traffic with Browser-Based RAT
articles.excerpt: The Chaos ransomware group is using a new Rust-based remote access trojan (RAT) called 'msaRAT' that cleverly evades network detection. A report from Cisco Talos explains that msaRAT routes its command-and-control (C2) communications through a legitimate, headless instance of Chrome or Edge. By using the Chrome DevTools Protocol and WebRTC, the malicious traffic is disguised as normal, encrypted browser activity, making it difficult for security tools to spot.

articles.headline: Check Point Patches Actively Exploited SmartConsole Auth Bypass Flaw
articles.title: Check Point Patches Critical Auth Bypass Flaw (CVE-2026-16232)
articles.excerpt: Check Point has issued an emergency hotfix for a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-16232, CVSS 9.3) in its SmartConsole management interface. The flaw, which is being actively exploited, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain full administrative access to internet-exposed Security Management servers. CISA has added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog, mandating federal agencies patch by July 25, 2026. Check Point has notified affected customers and urges all users to apply the patch immediately.

articles.headline: High-Severity Ubuntu Flaw Grants Local Users Full Root Access
articles.title: Ubuntu 'snap-confine' Flaw (CVE-2026-8933) Grants Root
articles.excerpt: A high-severity local privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-8933, CVSS 7.8) has been found in several default installations of Ubuntu Desktop. The flaw, discovered by Qualys, exists in the 'snap-confine' component of snapd. It allows any local, unprivileged user to exploit a race condition during sandbox creation to manipulate file operations and ultimately gain full root privileges on the system. Canonical has released a patch, and users are urged to update their systems.

articles.headline: CISA Adds SharePoint, Check Point Flaws to KEV Catalog
articles.title: CISA Adds Exploited SharePoint, Check Point Flaws to KEV
articles.excerpt: CISA has added two critical, actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The first is a Microsoft SharePoint Server deserialization flaw (CVE-2026-50522, CVSS 9.8), and the second is a Check Point SmartConsole authentication bypass (CVE-2026-16232, CVSS 9.3). The addition mandates U.S. federal agencies to patch these high-risk vulnerabilities by July 25, 2026, and serves as an urgent warning to all organizations.

articles.headline: Paidwork Data Breach Exposes Personal Data of 23 Million Users
articles.title: Paidwork Data Breach Exposes 23 Million Users' Data
articles.excerpt: The microtask platform Paidwork has suffered a massive data breach, exposing the sensitive personal and financial information of over 23 million users. The breach, which occurred in March 2026, was discovered after the stolen 11 GB database was put up for sale on a cybercrime forum. The exposed data includes full names, addresses, phone numbers, bank account details, and hashed passwords, creating a significant risk of identity theft and targeted fraud for the affected individuals.

articles.headline: Logistics Firm Warns of Rising Destructive Data-Wiping Attacks
articles.title: Source Logistics Warns of Destructive Data-Wiping Attacks
articles.excerpt: The third-party logistics provider Source Logistics has issued a public warning about the growing threat of destructive data-wiping cyberattacks. Citing the March 2026 attack on medical tech firm Stryker, where an Iranian hacktivist group wiped tens of thousands of devices, the warning highlights a shift from financial extortion to pure destruction. These attacks often abuse legitimate administrative tools like Microsoft Intune to issue remote wipe commands, making defense reliant on preventing credential compromise and limiting administrative access.
